sourceNote: The T-pose polar bear mesh (assets/models/polar-bear/README.md), with new quad faces on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist (polar-bear-arms.glb, tools/blender/polar_bear_arms.py) and on each leg from the haunch line to the ankle (tools/blender/polar_bear_legs.py). The new leg faces give a hollow behind the seated knee. The other faces stay unchanged.
heatSourceNote: Each vertex that the leg rebuild keeps takes the bone heat of this mesh, the copy before the rebuild, and only the new leg vertices take the bone heat of the source (kept_heat() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Thus the weights of the crotch do not move.
paintedNote: The weights of the trunk, the head, and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the Weight Paint fixes of tools/blender/polar_bear_arms.py, and the new leg vertices take the automatic weights of Blender (tools/blender/polar_bear_legs.py). The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights.

rootNormals.note: The faces near each knee joint and each wrist joint take the normals of the skin with no crease angle in the app (root_rim() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Their edges turn more than the crease angle of the app (40 degrees), so the skin normals make them shade soft. The claws keep their facets.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone of this length in units, which spans the three rings of its joint in the bind. The app turns them from the joints of the pose (poseArm() of src/models/studio-rig.ts).

name: Polar Bear

app.note: 1.5828 m for each unit, with the standing shoulder joints at 0.725 u. The legs keep the length of the mesh, so the trunk, the head, and the arms keep their meters. The reach is the reach of the arm factor.

armFactorNote: The arms keep the length of the mesh. Keep the limbs of the mesh, and fit the props.
legFactorNote: The thighs and the shins keep the length of the mesh, so that the body keeps the part ratios of the mesh: the legs from the crotch to the soles are 0.20 of the standing height. The bench and the piano fit the legs of the mesh.
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the skull top, the soles at y = 0, +z forward, +x the left side. The right side mirrors the left side. The thigh joint lies inside the haunch at y 0.28, so that the thigh is long enough to sit level. The arms are in a T-pose, with the palm down.

studio.note: The thighs slope 25 degrees down and 15 degrees out, and the shins are vertical, as in the seat of design 5.2, and the feet stand flat (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 15 0). The trunk keeps the seat of the source, and the play lean of the hold leans the spine, because a forward lean of the bind folds both arms.

armFree.note: The arm of the T-pose is free of the trunk beyond x 0.145. A vertex of the free arm lies beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, within radius of the chain of the arm joints, and above the floor.

line.note: The angle of the other meshes: a lower angle mixes the weights of long arm faces.

knee.note: Each vertex splits its weight of the thigh and the shin by its height: the thigh share grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, around the knee joint. Thus each ring of the quad tube of a leg takes one share, and the dual quaternion blend of the knee (bind.knee) turns it by that share of the bend.

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the rump stays on the bench and the thigh turns as one tube from the haunch to the knee.

weights.rigidNote: Each pair of thin faces of the front of the right hip and the right groin, where the thigh meets the belly, takes one mean of the weights of its corners, so that the faces do not fold when the pedal leg turns.
weights.note: Beyond the plane of armSplit (armFree), only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom, each vertex follows the head only. armTop starts above the top of the level arms of the T-pose (y 0.79). Each ear follows its ear bone above earBase. The short tail is a ball on one bone (tailBall).

flip.note: The values of the other meshes.

check.note: The values of the other meshes.

shift.note: The fur of the mesh is cream, so each fur face with a chroma and a lightness above the ramps takes 1.045 of its lightness and 0.3 of its chroma, toward the white of polar-bear-views.png and SPECIES_COLORS. The black nose, eyes, and claws keep their colors.

colors.note: The color shift moves the cream fur toward the white of the reference. The dark limit keeps the fur out of the dark faces.

eyeShell.note: The values of the other meshes.

chair.note: The seat is the piano bench of the pianist (prop): it is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The front edge lies 0.015 units behind the hip joints, and the back edge at the back of the haunch (benchFitOf() of tools/studio-body.ts, StudioBody.benchDepth).

crease.note: 12 rounds, so that no face of the hips stays turned over in the bind under the thighs.

kneeCrease.note: Each vertex within reach units of the seam on the inner side of the knee moves half of the way to the middle of its neighbors in each of 4 rounds, times a weight that falls from 1 on the seam to 0 at reach (knee_relax() and seam_relax() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). Thus the crease shows no dark flaps, and the knee keeps most of its width.

sit.note: The values of the dog and the deer, with 8 rounds of smoothing, so that no face of the hips stays turned over in the bind.

bind.note: Each vertex with a weight on both the thigh and the shin of one side takes the dual quaternion blend in the seated bind (bind_skin() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py), so that each ring of the knee keeps its radius: the knee front rounds over the kneecap. The other vertices keep the linear blend, and the app moves the bind mesh with the linear blend.
